purpose: Audit why the D265 overexpansion selector recovers final examples that D262 misses but regresses one D262 success, before designing a conditional gate or buying labels.
findings: D265 recovers 2 D262 misses but regresses 1 D262 success, which explains the net +1 final selection and the scalar-hybrid failure.
The regression has higher entity/list-scope risk than the recovered cases, so a low-risk activation gate is plausible.
2 examples still fail under both D262 and D265, so even a good gate will not be paper-sufficient without a broader target or stronger adjudicator.

proposed_gate.name: overexpansion_rescue_when_supported_candidate_has_low_scope_risk
proposed_gate.candidate_rule_from_diagnostic_only: Use D265 only as a rescue signal when the overexpansion-selected candidate is short, has no extra entity/list-scope risk, and D262's top candidate has judge-like unsupported-claim pattern proxies.
proposed_gate.zero_cost_next_step: Implement the gate on non-final validation first using D264 features and D262/D265 scores; then evaluate final diagnostics without tuning on them.

decision.next_step: Build a leakage-safe non-final gate that activates the overexpansion score only for short low-risk candidates and rejects cases like the D265 regression on 2004.04060.
decision.reason: D265 has two final rescues and one final regression; a scalar hybrid loses the rescues, so the missing piece is conditional activation rather than more broad labels.

llm_budget.note: This audit reads existing final diagnostic artifacts only.
